# Heuristic Over Exact Max-Cut

**Decision.** Solve Max-Cut with best-improvement local search plus ten random restarts, instead of
searching the partition space exhaustively.

**Date.** 2026-03-20, the first lab committed to
[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]].

## Why

The rejected alternative is quantified in the lab itself: with 127 vertices the space of partitions
is **`2^127`**. That number is not a rhetorical flourish — it is the argument, and the lab reports it
rather than leaving "intractable" as an adjective.

> "The thread running through all six: take a formal object (a cut, a modulus, a set, a recursion, a
> graph, an information system) and make its behaviour **observable**."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-10

Stating the size of the space you are *not* searching is what makes the heuristic legible as a
choice — see [[make-the-formal-object-observable]] and [[max-cut-and-local-search]].

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Exhaustive enumeration** | `2^127` partitions |
| **Exact solver** (ILP / branch-and-bound) | a dependency and a modelling layer, for a lab about the algorithm |
| **Goemans–Williamson SDP** | 0.878-approximation *with a proof*, but needs an SDP solver — no dependency in this repo is heavier than matplotlib |
| **Single-start local search** | one descent lands wherever its start drains to; the restarts are the whole improvement |

**TODO:** none of these rejections is written down in the repo. Only the `2^127` figure and a commit
message, `Add conclusion about multi-start heuristic effectiveness` (2026-03-20), evidence the
reasoning. The table above states what the alternatives *are*; it does not claim they were

implemented.

## What was given up

An approximation **guarantee**. Multi-start local search has no proven ratio — the result is "the
best of ten local optima", which could be far from optimal on an adversarial instance and there is no
bound saying otherwise. The lab has no comparison against a known optimum or a published bound, so
solution quality is unmeasured. **TODO:** `confidence: low` on any effectiveness claim.

This is the same species of trade as the one on [[shortest-path-algorithm-family]], where a function
named `tspChristofides` gives up the 1.5-approximation guarantee by matching greedily — with the
difference that here the loss of guarantee is deliberate and there it is unremarked.
